title: Fasteners and threads
summary: Look-up tables for metric and imperial coarse threads: pitch, tap drill, clearance hole, wrench size, strength markings and dry tightening torque. Also covers telling metric from imperial and the basics of wood screws and nails.

steps.text: Measure the bolt diameter with calipers and the pitch with a thread gauge, to tell metric (pitch in mm) from imperial (threads per inch).
steps.warn: Do not mix metric and imperial parts, even when the sizes look close.

steps.text: Find the size in the thread table for tap drill, clearance hole and wrench size.
Read the head mark (lines, or a number such as 8.8) for the strength grade, then take the dry torque from the matching column.
steps.warn: Use the maker's torque for wheels, brakes, steering, engines and lifting gear. Cut the value for oiled threads.

steps.text: For wood, use the screw and nail notes and drill a lead hole in hardwood or near an edge.

notes:
Use the maker's torque and fastener spec whenever you have it. The values here are general figures for common steel bolts.

## Metric or imperial?
- Metric is written M8 x 1.25: 8 mm diameter, 1.25 mm pitch (gap between threads). Imperial is written 1/2"-13: diameter, then threads per inch (TPI). (Mutual Screw)
- Measure the diameter with calipers, then the pitch with a thread gauge. Pitch in mm = 25.4 / TPI, so 1/4"-20 is 1.27 mm and M6 is 1.0 mm. (Mutual Screw)
- Sizes can be close: M6 is about 1/4 in, M8 about 5/16 in, M10 about 3/8 in, M12 about 1/2 in. They are not interchangeable. Never mix them in one joint. (Mutual Screw)

## Metric coarse threads

| Size | Pitch (mm) | Tap drill (mm) | Clearance hole (mm) | Wrench, ISO / DIN (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M3 | 0.50 | 2.5 | 3.3 | not confirmed |
| M4 | 0.70 | 3.3 | 4.4 | 7 / 7 |
| M5 | 0.80 | 4.2 | 5.5 | 8 / 8 |
| M6 | 1.00 | 5.0 | 6.6 | 10 / 10 |
| M8 | 1.25 | 6.8 | 8.8 | 13 / 13 |
| M10 | 1.50 | 8.5 | 11.0 | 16 / 17 |
| M12 | 1.75 | 10.2 to 10.3 | 13.2 | 18 / 19 |

Pitch (Engineering ToolBox). Drills give about 75% thread engagement; clearance is the "free" fit (Penn). Wrench size is across flats; M10 and M12 bolts may take the DIN size, so try both (Zipp Group).

## Imperial coarse threads (UNC)

| Size | TPI | Tap drill (in) | Clearance hole (in) | Wrench (in) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #4-40 | 40 | #43 (0.089) | #30 (0.1285) | - |
| #6-32 | 32 | #36 (0.1065) | #25 (0.1495) | - |
| #8-32 | 32 | #29 (0.136) | #16 (0.177) | - |
| #10-24 | 24 | #25 (0.1495) | #7 (0.201) | - |
| 1/4-20 | 20 | #7 (0.201) | H (0.266) | 7/16 (or 3/8) |
| 5/16-18 | 18 | F (0.257) | Q (0.332) | 1/2 |
| 3/8-16 | 16 | 5/16 (0.3125) | X (0.397) | 9/16 |
| 1/2-13 | 13 | 27/64 (0.4219) | 17/32 (0.5312) | 3/4 |

TPI and wrench sizes (Engineering ToolBox, hex bolts to ANSI/ASME B18.2.1); drills (Penn). Number and letter drills are listed with their decimal inch size. Major diameters: #4 0.112, #6 0.138, #8 0.164, #10 0.190 in (Engineering ToolBox).

## Bolt strength markings

| Head mark | Grade | Min tensile | Min yield |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | SAE 2 | 60,000 to 74,000 psi | 36,000 to 57,000 psi |
| 3 lines | SAE 5 | 120,000 psi (about 830 MPa) | 92,000 psi (about 630 MPa) |
| 6 lines | SAE 8 | 150,000 psi (about 1,030 MPa) | 130,000 psi (about 900 MPa) |
| 8.8 | Metric | 800 MPa | 640 MPa |
| 10.9 | Metric | 1,040 MPa | 940 MPa |
| 12.9 | Metric | 1,220 MPa | 1,100 MPa |

SAE (Mutual Screw); metric (TR Fastenings).
- SAE: number of lines + 2 = grade. Metric: the class is stamped on the head. First number x 100 = nominal tensile strength in MPa; first x second x 10 = nominal yield in MPa. The minimums for 10.9 and 12.9 are a little higher than this formula gives. (AIMS)
- Rough matches: SAE 2 is about 4.6, SAE 5 about 8.8, SAE 8 about 10.9. Do not swap by match alone. (AIMS)
- Replace bolts like for like. (Atlas Copco)

## Tightening torque (dry)
**Conditions:** clean, dry, uncoated steel threads, K = 0.20, calculated at 75% of proof load. Maker's specification takes priority. (AIMS)

| Metric size | 8.8 (N·m) | 10.9 (N·m) | 12.9 (N·m) |
|---|---|---|---|
| M4 | 3.2 | 4.4 | 5.1 |
| M5 | 6.4 | 8.8 | 10 |
| M6 | 11 | 15 | 18 |
| M8 | 26 | 37 | 43 |
| M10 | 52 | 72 | 84 |
| M12 | 91 | 126 | 147 |

| Imperial size | SAE 2 (ft-lb) | SAE 5 (ft-lb) | SAE 8 (ft-lb) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1/4-20 | 5.5 | 8.4 | 11.9 |
| 5/16-18 | 11.3 | 17.4 | 24.6 |
| 3/8-16 | 20.0 | 30.9 | 43.6 |
| 7/16-14 | 32.0 | 49.4 | 69.8 |
| 1/2-13 | 48.8 | 75.4 | 106.4 |

- Multiply by 0.75 for lightly oiled threads, 1.25 for hot-dip galvanised, 0.65 for copper anti-seize or molybdenum grease. Using the dry value on oiled threads over-tightens. (AIMS)
- 1 ft-lb = 1.356 N·m.
- Wheels, brakes, steering, engines and lifting gear: use the maker's value only.

## Wood screws and nails
- Screw gauge diameters: #6 0.138 in (3.5 mm), #8 0.164 in (4.2 mm), #10 0.190 in (4.8 mm). Higher number = thicker. (HandySkook)
- Screw root diameter is about two-thirds of the shank. The Wood Handbook's holding figures assume a lead hole of about 70% of the root in softwood and about 90% in hardwood. Soap on the thread eases driving in dense wood. (USDA FPL)
- Screws in end grain hold about 75% as well as in side grain. (USDA FPL)

| Nail (common) | Length, in (mm) | Diameter, in (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| 6d | 2 (50.8) | 0.113 (2.87) |
| 8d | 2-1/2 (63.5) | 0.131 (3.33) |
| 10d | 3 (76.2) | 0.148 (3.76) |
| 16d | 3-1/2 (88.9) | 0.162 (4.11) |
| 20d | 4 (101.6) | 0.192 (4.88) |

(USDA FPL) Penny sizes are obsolete and imports may not match; specify length and diameter. Box nails are thinner and ring or spiral nails are thinner than common nails of the same size. A lead hole of about 90% of the nail diameter cuts splitting. For toenailing, drive at 30°, starting about one-third of the nail length from the end.
